description: Fix 1b: speed. Confirm the ONNX session is created ONCE and warmed (verify current behavior first), confirm the decision-prompt token budget is applied on the hot path for large real pages, and add an int8 QUANTIZATION path to scripts/prepare-model.sh with a real CPU fp32-vs-int8 decision-ms measurement behind LAYA_MODEL_DIR. If int8 quantization of this ModernBERT-shaped graph is not feasible, document precisely why (failing command + error) and skip it - partial verified progress beats nothing. NOTE: the GPU speedup itself is UNVERIFIABLE here (no GPU); this feature is about the CPU-measurable speed levers only.
steps: VERIFY FIRST, do not assume. (a) Session-once: read node_modules/@receptron/laya/dist/laya.js and src/laya/engine.ts and confirm Laya.load creates the ort InferenceSession exactly once and LayaEngine reuses it across decide() calls (it does - Laya holds `session`; decide calls systemOne on the same handle). Record the evidence. If a warmup pass would measurably help cold-start, note it, but do NOT add a warmup that duplicates the model load. (b) Token budget on the hot path: read src/state-builder.ts and confirm buildState clamps visibleText (stateTextLimit, default 1200, bounds 200..8000) and caps controls, and that renderState (used by engine.decide) consumes that clamped state. Confirm the budget is actually applied on the decide hot path (not only on the escalation prompt). Record findings; only change code if a gap is found.

Add an int8 quantization path to scripts/prepare-model.sh. Add a third mode (e.g. `scripts/prepare-model.sh int8 [OUT_DIR]` or a `--int8` flag on the web-agent path) that, after producing the fp32 ONNX bundle, runs onnxruntime dynamic quantization (`from onnxruntime.quantization import quantize_dynamic, QuantType`; QuantType.QInt8) over laya.onnx to produce an int8 laya.onnx in a sibling bundle dir, copying the tokenizer + laya_config.json unchanged so it is a drop-in LAYA_MODEL_DIR. Reuse the existing `uv` Python 3.12 venv setup already in the script. Keep NO EM DASHES in the script prose. Never commit the produced weights (.gitignore already excludes *.onnx / *.onnx.data / model/ / .venv / .cache).

MEASURE with real weights on CPU (this is the honest, measurable deliverable). In a scratch dir OUTSIDE the tracked tree: build the fp32 bundle (`scripts/prepare-model.sh web-agent <scratch>` or `reference`), then build the int8 bundle. Run the product's own decide path for each (e.g. `LAYA_MODEL_DIR=<fp32> pnpm test` for the gated real-weights tests, and a small timing probe of LayaEngine.decide median ms, mirroring how PLAN.md's FEAT-003 block measured ~440-490 ms web-agent / ~810-870 ms reference on CPU). Capture fp32-vs-int8 median decision-ms and any accuracy/output sanity delta. Paste the REAL numbers into this feature's findings.

If dynamic int8 quantization of this ModernBERT-shaped graph FAILS or produces a broken/incompatible bundle (e.g. @receptron/laya cannot load it, or ort rejects an op), STOP that sub-path: record the exact failing command and the full error text in findings, mark the int8 sub-path documented-and-skipped (retryable false for int8 only), and keep the rest of the feature (session-once + token-budget verification) done. Do not fake a number.

Clean up ALL scratch weights/venv/download artifacts before finishing (`git status --porcelain --ignored` must be clean of *.onnx / *.onnx.data / model/ / .venv / .cache). The offline stub suite must stay green with NO weights.
acceptance_criteria: Written confirmation (with code evidence) that the ONNX session is created once and reused across decisions, and that the state token budget (stateTextLimit) is applied on the decide hot path.

scripts/prepare-model.sh has an int8 quantization path that produces a drop-in LAYA_MODEL_DIR bundle, OR the int8 sub-path is documented-and-skipped with the exact failing command + error if the graph cannot be quantized.
A REAL CPU fp32-vs-int8 median decision-ms measurement is recorded in findings (or, if int8 is infeasible, the precise blocker is recorded). No fabricated numbers.
No weights/venv/scratch artifacts are committed; git status --ignored is clean of them. Offline stub suite stays green with no weights.
pnpm run typecheck clean, pnpm run build exit 0, pnpm test green (offline, no weights).
verification: bash -lc 'pnpm test' (offline, no weights, stays green)

int8_subpath.detail: int8 dynamic quantization of the exported web-agent (ModernBERT-shaped) graph is INFEASIBLE with onnxruntime 1.30.0 / onnx 1.23.0 in this environment. The fp32 bundle exports and loads/runs correctly, but onnxruntime's quantize_dynamic aborts before writing any output because its internal save_and_reload_model_with_shape_infer -> onnx.shape_inference rejects the graph. Failing command (as wired into scripts/prepare-model.sh int8): from onnxruntime.quantization import quantize_dynamic, QuantType; quantize_dynamic(model_input='webagent-onnx/laya.onnx', model_output='webagent-onnx-int8/laya.onnx', weight_type=QuantType.QInt8). Full error: onnx.onnx_cpp2py_export.shape_inference.InferenceError: [ShapeInferenceError] Inferred shape and existing shape differ in dimension 0: (772) vs (256). Confirmed NOT a missing-preprocessing issue: onnxruntime.quantization.shape_inference.quant_pre_process(..., skip_symbolic_shape=True) SUCCEEDS on the same model, but quantize_dynamic re-runs strict shape inference internally and fails identically on the preprocessed model. The (772) vs (256) mismatch is a shape annotation the torch.onnx exporter emits for this ModernBERT attention graph that ONNX strict shape inference will not accept. The scripts/prepare-model.sh int8 scaffolding (fp32 build + QuantType.QInt8 quantize_dynamic + tokenizer/laya_config copy) is kept intact so it works once a compatible export or an onnxruntime version that tolerates this graph is available. No int8 number was fabricated.

findings:
PART 1 (VERIFIED, no code change needed - the existing code already satisfies both requirements):
(a) SESSION-ONCE, reused across decisions. node_modules/@receptron/laya/dist/laya.js: Laya.load() calls ort.InferenceSession.create(path.join(modelDir,'laya.onnx'), {...}) EXACTLY ONCE and stores it on `this.session`; systemOne() calls this.session.run(...) on that same handle; close() calls this.session.release(). src/laya/engine.ts: LayaEngine wraps ONE Laya instance created once in the async LayaEngine.load(); LayaEngine.decide() calls this.laya.systemOne(rendered, questions) - it never re-loads. The factory src/laya/index.ts createEngine()/resolveEngine() loads the model exactly once (a candidate EP probe IS the single load attempt). So the session is created once and reused for every decide(). No warmup that duplicates the model load was added (correct per the plan). Cold start is the one-time Laya.load (~seconds for the 1291 MB bundle); a decide-level warmup would only re-run the already-warm session, so none is warranted; the probe below discards 3 warmup decides purely for measurement stability.
(b) TOKEN BUDGET ON THE DECIDE HOT PATH. Chain: src/config.ts parses stateTextLimit (DEFAULT_STATE_TEXT_LIMIT=1200, clamped to STATE_TEXT_LIMIT_MIN=200..STATE_TEXT_LIMIT_MAX=8000, env LAYA_STATE_TEXT_LIMIT) -> src/server.ts threads config.stateTextLimit into the run_goal ctx -> src/tools/run_goal.ts maps ctx.stateTextLimit to stateOptions.maxVisibleText -> src/autopilot/loop.ts line 1519 calls buildState(goal, snapshot, recentActions, stateOptions) on the DECIDE hot path (not just escalation) -> src/state-builder.ts buildState clamps visibleText via maxVisibleText (default 1200) AND caps controls via maxControls (RECOMMENDED_MAX_OPTIONS=20) and maxOptionLen -> engine.decide() calls renderState(state) which serializes exactly that clamped visibleText + capped numbered controls and feeds it to laya.systemOne. Confirmed by test/tier1-token-latency.test.ts (buildState with maxVisibleText:500 yields visibleText.length <= 501 incl. ellipsis) and test/config.test.ts (stateTextLimit default 1200, LAYA_STATE_TEXT_LIMIT parse/clamp). So the budget is applied on the hot path. No gap; no code change.

PART 2 (DONE): scripts/prepare-model.sh gained a third mode `int8 [OUT_DIR]`. It refactors the web-agent fp32 export into a reusable build_web_agent_fp32() helper (venv, HF download, export_onnx.py, tokenizer special-token rename) reused by both `web-agent` and `int8`. The `int8` mode then runs onnxruntime dynamic quantization (from onnxruntime.quantization import quantize_dynamic, QuantType; QuantType.QInt8) over laya.onnx into a SIBLING webagent-onnx-int8/ dir, copying tokenizer/ and laya_config.json unchanged so it is a drop-in LAYA_MODEL_DIR. Reuses the existing uv Python 3.12 venv. bash -n clean; no em dashes. See int8_subpath: the quantization step itself is infeasible on this graph/onnxruntime, so the mode's scaffolding is verified-present but its output cannot be produced here.

PART 3 (MEASURED, REAL CPU, this session, Node 22.23.2, 8 CPUs):
- fp32 web-agent bundle built via `scripts/prepare-model.sh int8 <scratch>`: export parity max|dlogits|=0.00054, max|dact|=0.0; laya.onnx 1291 MB (weights inline); tokenizer rename applied.
- Gated real-weights test: LAYA_MODEL_DIR=<fp32> pnpm exec vitest run test/autopilot.test.ts -> 16 passed, incl. 'Autopilot with real Laya weights ... drives the search form to a verified result using the on-device model' (4475 ms) - real INDEPENDENT final-page verification, not just a DONE decision. (The libonnxruntime_providers_shared.so CUDA warning is expected: no GPU here, resolver falls through to CPU.)
- fp32 median decision-ms probe (LayaEngine.decide, realistic clamped search-page PageState, 3 warmup + 15 timed): median 407 ms, min 396 ms, max 419 ms. Deterministic output across runs: operation SELECT (opConf 0.4014), target e2 (targetConf 0.5815). This extends PLAN.md's FEAT-003 web-agent ~440-490 ms CPU figure (in-range, slightly faster on this 8-CPU box).
- int8 vs fp32 comparison: NOT AVAILABLE because int8 quantization is infeasible on this graph (see int8_subpath). No int8 number fabricated.

CLEANUP + VERIFICATION: all scratch weights/venv/probe removed (rm -rf .cache). git status --porcelain --ignored shows NO *.onnx/*.onnx.data/model/.venv/.cache (only dist/, node_modules/, .playwright-mcp/, benchmark/node_modules/ ignored + the two intended tracked edits). Offline suite green WITHOUT weights: pnpm run typecheck clean, pnpm run build exit 0, pnpm test = 322 passed / 3 skipped.
